findings: commercial:grin is presented on its official homepage as 'Creator marketing for brands' and runs gifting, affiliate, and paid programs for brands; it is brand-side influencer marketing, not the creator-side sponsorship management system required by creator-sponsorship-management.

commercial:greenfly is presented on its official homepage as high-performance content operations for sports/entertainment; its center of gravity is content capture, organization, distribution, and measurement, not persistent fan profiles plus organization-run engagement activities with participation captured back into fan records as required by fan-engagement-platform.
non_blocking_notes: Commercial entries were reviewed at the required basic authenticity/type-match level; homepages such as Resy and BlueCart are marketing-oriented and do not detail every backend workflow, but they are not treated as failures under the commercial standard.

Open-source entries were reviewed from repository metadata plus license snapshots; README or deployment documentation was not captured in this batch, so core-workflow proof is at metadata-description level rather than full implementation documentation.
Insufficient-evidence leaves are correctly left case-less and archived false; no additional rejection is warranted for those leaves.

limits: Independent first-pass review only; collector and reviewer used the same Beam Free model, so review independence is weaker than a cross-model review. Review was read-only and based on the provided batch, research, and source snapshots without new network fetches or file writes. Commercial entries were judged on basic authenticity and type match only; open-source entries were judged from repository metadata plus license snapshots.
